The vertical asymptote gives −a=2, so a=−2. Since (5,0) lies on the graph, 1+b=0, so b=−1 and ab=2.
ㄱ is false because 45°=π/4. 300° and 60° are x-axis reflections; −5π/6 is coterminal with 7π/6 in quadrant III.
sinθ·tanθ>0 implies cosθ>0. Then sinθ+tanθ=sinθ(1+1/cosθ)<0 forces sinθ<0, so θ is in quadrant IV; only 11π/3 qualifies.
The logarithm argument is positive for −2<x<5. The base |x−2| must be positive and not 1, excluding x=2,1,3. The remaining integers −1,0,4 sum to 3.
For every x<0, B^x>1 exactly when 0<B<1, where B=((a−4)^2+1)/2. This requires (a−4)^2<1, so the only integer a is 4.
The domain is −4<x<7. Combining logs gives (7−x)(x+4)≤10, equivalent to (x−6)(x+3)≥0. The eligible integers are −3 and 6, whose sum is 3.
The point condition gives 6+c=10, so c=4. Shifting right by d=(1/2)log₃5 changes 2/9^x to 2·9^d/9^x=10/9^x; shifting up by 7 gives a=10 and b=11. Thus a+b+c=25.
The speed ratio is 1.5, so LA−LB=28log(vA/vB)=28log(3/2)=28(log3−log2).
Writing c=cosθ, the denominator simplifies to c(1+3c), so the given quotient is tanθ=3. In quadrant III, (sinθ,cosθ)=(-3/√10,-1/√10), hence sinθ−cosθ=−2/√10=−√10/5.
The inequality 16·2^(t/2)>4096·2^(−t/4) reduces to 3t/4>8, or t>32/3. The least natural t is 11.
At P=(1/4,1/4), the curves give Q=(1,1/4) and R=(1/4,1). Thus PQ=PR=3/4, satisfying the condition; QR=√((3/4)^2+(3/4)^2)=3√2/4.

Set t=(1/3)^x>0. The inequality becomes t²−6kt+18k≤0. For k<0 the expression is negative for small positive t; for k≥2 it is nonpositive at a positive t. For 0≤k<2 its minimum over t>0 is positive (or t²>0 when k=0), so no solution exists.

The sector-area condition gives AC²+BC²=AB², so ABC is right. Its integer legs have product 60 and area 30, yielding the 5–12–13 triangle. The total arc condition gives θ=12π/30=2π/5, so S₃=(1/2)(2π/5)(13²)=169π/5.
For radius R=3^(2/n), tangent-intercept triangle area is Sₙ=R⁴/(2|x₁y₁|)=1/2·3^(8/n+2n−3). The exponent is minimized over natural n at n=2, giving m=243/2 and k+m=247/2.
Collinearity gives a=2^u,b=2^(4u),c=2^(5u); b−a=14 yields a=2,b=16,c=32. Put X=log₂p,Y=log₂q. Then 1/X+4/Y=1. Minimizing X+Y gives X=3,Y=6, so the minimum is 9.

For each n=1,…,4, compare the tent graph with g and h on their domains. Monotonicity/concavity on each tent branch gives g-intersection counts 0,0,3,1 and h-intersection counts 0,1,1,1. Therefore a=4,b=3 and a+b=7.
For (abc)^n to be integral, n/3, n/5, and n/9 must all be integers because 3,7,11 are distinct primes. The least such n is lcm(3,5,9)=45.

The quadratic −x²−8x+9=25−(x+4)² has maximum 25 on the stated interval. If a>1, log_a is increasing and the maximum value 2 gives a²=25, hence a=5. If 0<a<1, the maximum comes from the minimum quadratic value 9, which would require a²=9 and contradict a<1.
For n=4,…,10, the values of f(n) are 2,1,0,1,0,1,2. The strict increase occurs at n=6,8,9, whose sum is 23.

Let t=(1/2)^x>0. The equation requires |t−a|+b=3 or 7. Counting positive t solutions for natural a,b≤10 gives exactly three roots for 4 pairs when b=1, 4 pairs when b=2, and 6 pairs when b=3; no other b gives three. Total 14, which is absent from the listed choices.
